category_title: Students in an inclusive urban classroom exhibiting high-frequency disruptive behaviors and low academic engagement
minimal_context: The student is navigating the classroom to retrieve supplies from the teacher's desk and access the computer area for independent work.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for independent work. Please walk to my desk to get your supplies and reading books, or go to the computer area.

STUDENT: (Leaves seat and walks through the undefined pathway, pushing another student) Move out of my way!

TUTOR: Please walk quietly and get your materials.

STUDENT: (Stops at the computers facing the classroom, ignoring the teacher's direction) Hey, look at what is on this screen!

TUTOR: You need to get your supplies from my desk and go to your seat.

STUDENT: (Walks to the congested teacher's desk, hits another student reaching for the same supplies, and throws a marker across the room) Back off, I was here first! I'm not doing this!

options.A: Have the student complete reflective journal entries, encouraging them to write or draw freely.
options.B: Offer options for independent work topics with open-ended format possibilities for presenting their knowledge.
options.C: Adhere to a routine, providing positive reinforcement for desired behaviors (e.g., social praise, stickers).
options.D: Move the supplies and independent reading books to the middle of the classroom.
